analysis:
Examined both PlannedDisconnect revisions, Serve metadata and all supplied patch/base excerpts. PlannedDisconnect head lines 13–22 prevent ordinary disconnect fencing under an add-on hold while retaining inflight drain, acknowledgement, generation and cancellation checks. Lines 39–40 and 77–81 allow planned reconnects beneath the hold; lines 90–100 and 120–128 restore hold state and preserve reconnect fencing on release. Serve head patch lines 74–78 starts hold handling before local serving/preload; startup guards now distinguish service changes from holds so registration and connection controls remain alive.
No concrete regression is established in this scope. Security hardening, registration key/attestation binding, encrypted request plumbing and connection-authorization invalidation are not changed by the supplied Serve patch (base lines 140–213, 323–349, 401–427). Cache maintenance and cryptographic policy are unchanged here (T-041); no new plaintext, credential or billing exposure is visible.
Integration must verify the new hold service and ServingDrain implementation: beginServingDrain/resumeReconnect must preserve hold ownership, refusingForServiceChange must still stop lifecycle/update changes, and local/coordinator admissions and startup/background model loads must honor the hold. Relevant paths are PlannedDisconnect head lines 47, 71–74, 96–100 and 120–128, and Serve's startup preload/local endpoint calls (base lines 99–126). Also check hold takeover while acknowledgeDrain is suspended (head lines 20–22): release or reconnect must not strand a permanently fenced socket. These contracts are outside the supplied source, not observed missing controls. Review them against TB-002, TB-007 and T-053, including fresh-session authorization and accepted-work accounting; no new trust grant is visible here.
